import sys, json

# The MENU of this library (GH #950): asked on `in_schemas` with the names a
# collector declares, it answers the declaration of every `lib_*` tool it
# serves and names every other name in `unknown` -- the answer shape of the
# file space's menu, byte for byte, so a collector merges it as one more
# answerer (`context.tool_answerer` 'library', stamped by the member). `*` asks
# for all four.
# --8<-- lib-offer
# THE LIBRARY TOOLS, one list, one entry per tool (GH #950). It stands WORD FOR
# WORD in `./schemas` (which hands it to a model's menu) and in `./tools` (which
# checks every call against it before a question leaves), because a code cell
# has no library it could share. The name IS the mapping: `lib_<op>` asks the
# op `<op>` on `in_lib`; no other rule exists.
#
# Every description says the two things a model needs to go on: the address a
# hit carries (`fh-<12 hex>` for a file, `fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>` for an item in
# it), and that `file_read` with that address reads the span -- the library
# finds, the file space reads. There is no writing tool here.
LIMIT = {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 20,
         "description": "the most hits on one page (20 by default)"}
CURSOR = {"type": "string", "description": "the `next` of the page before"}
DEPTH = {"type": "integer", "minimum": 1, "maximum": 3}


def _obj(props, required):
    return {"type": "object", "properties": props, "required": required,
            "additionalProperties": False}


LIB_OFFER = [
    {"name": "lib_find",
     "description": "Find files of this knowledge space by words -- in their path, the names "
                    "of their functions, classes or sections, their summary line and tags -- "
                    "best first, each with its address `fh-<12 hex>`, path, kind, summary line "
                    "and `why` it matched. `file_read` on that address (or on an item of it, "
                    "`fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>` from `file_outline`) reads the span; `next` is the "
                    "`cursor` of the next page.",
     "parameters": _obj({"q": {"type": "string", "description": "the words to look for"},
                         "kind": {"type": "string", "description": "only files of this kind"},
                         "fmt": {"type": "string",
                                 "description": "only files of this format: `python`, `rust`, `markdown`, `json`, `toml` or `pdf`"},
                         "under": {"type": "string",
                                   "description": "only files under this folder, like `/src`"},
                         "limit": LIMIT, "cursor": CURSOR}, ["q"])},
    {"name": "lib_symbol",
     "description": "Find where a name is defined: a function, class, module or section, "
                    "bare (`load`) or qualified (`pkg.mod:load`), each hit with its address "
                    "`fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>`, the path of its file and its summary line. "
                    "`file_read` with that address reads exactly that span.",
     "parameters": _obj({"name": {"type": "string", "description": "the name to look up"},
                         "limit": LIMIT, "cursor": CURSOR}, ["name"])},
    {"name": "lib_related",
     "description": "What is connected to an address `fh-<12 hex>` or `fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>`: "
                    "its `callers`, its `dependents` (up to `depth` 3), its `deps`, or files "
                    "`similar` by meaning; each hit with its address, path and summary line. "
                    "`file_read` with a hit's address reads its span.",
     "parameters": _obj({"addr": {"type": "string",
                                  "description": "`fh-<12 hex>` or `fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>`"},
                         "how": {"type": "string",
                                 "enum": ["callers", "dependents", "deps", "similar"]},
                         "depth": DEPTH, "limit": LIMIT, "cursor": CURSOR},
                        ["addr", "how"])},
    {"name": "lib_tree",
     "description": "The folders and files under a folder `under` (`/` by default), `depth` "
                    "levels deep (1 to 3), ordered by path, each file with its address "
                    "`fh-<12 hex>`; `file_read` on that address (or on an item of it, "
                    "`fh-<12 hex>#<anchor>` from `file_outline`) reads the span; `next` is the "
                    "`cursor` of the next page.",
     "parameters": _obj({"under": {"type": "string", "description": "a folder, `/` by default"},
                         "depth": DEPTH, "limit": LIMIT, "cursor": CURSOR}, [])},
]
# --8<-- end lib-offer


doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
asked = (doc.get("body") or {}).get("tools")
if not isinstance(asked, list):
    # ABSENT and EMPTY are two requests: a caller that declared nothing gets
    # nothing, a request that lost its list is told so.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "schemas", "error_code": "tools_missing",
                   "schema_count": 0, "unknown_count": 0},
        "schemas": [], "unknown": [], "sidecar": [], "messages": []}))
    sys.exit(0)

served = [t["name"] for t in LIB_OFFER]
names = [str(n) for n in asked if isinstance(n, str)]
if "*" in names:
    wanted, unknown = list(served), []
else:
    seen, wanted, unknown = set(), [], []
    for n in names:
        if n in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(n)
        (wanted if n in served else unknown).append(n)
by_name = {t["name"]: t for t in LIB_OFFER}
schemas = [{"name": n, "description": by_name[n]["description"],
            "parameters": by_name[n]["parameters"]} for n in wanted]
header = {"operation": "schemas", "schema_count": len(schemas),
          "unknown_count": len(unknown)}
if unknown:
    header["error_code"] = "tool_unknown"
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"header": header, "schemas": schemas, "unknown": unknown,
                             "sidecar": [], "messages": []}))

description.purpose: The menu of this library: asked with the tool names a collector declares, it answers `{name, description, parameters}` for every `lib_*` tool it serves and names every other name in `unknown` -- the answer shape of the file space's menu, so a collector merges it as one more answerer. `*` asks for all four tools, every one of them a read.
description.use_when: Reached on this hive's `in_schemas` lane, on an asking collector's menu tick. Never part of a tool round.
description.not_in_scope: No write tool and no sidecar section: a library asks a model for nothing in return.
description.emits_meaning: schemas[]: one declaration per asked name this library serves, in the order asked (`*` in menu order). unknown[]: the names it does not serve, verbatim; hop.error_code `tool_unknown` then, `tools_missing` when the request carried no `tools` list. sidecar[] is always empty.
description.consumes_meaning: A menu question: `tools`, the names the asking collector declares.
